abstract: Spatial omics enable the in situ characterization of tissue architecture by measuring molecular modalities. However, integrating these datasets remains challenging due to differences in spatial resolution, cross-modal alignment and molecular coverage. Here we show that Cross-scale spatial Omics Registration and Analysis via graph Learning (CORAL), a probabilistic deep generative model, leverages graph attention to integrate diverse spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic data across spatial scales. CORAL jointly models high-resolution datasets with limited molecular coverage and low-resolution genome-wide datasets, generating unified representations with broad molecular coverage and high spatial resolution. Across synthetic and experimental datasets from diverse tissues and platforms, CORAL accurately identifies spatial domains, predicts high-resolution molecular profiles, detects spatially variable genes and infers cell-cell interactions. Applied to spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data from hepatocellular carcinoma patients before and after immunotherapy, CORAL identified organized immune-cell subsets and signaling pathways associated with therapeutic resistance. These results demonstrate CORAL's broad applicability for resolving tissue organization and clinically relevant multicellular interactions.
